text: The Hubble tension is the statistically significant (> 5σ) discrepancy between the present‑day expansion rate of the Universe (the Hubble constant, H₀) measured locally and the value inferred from early‑Universe observations. Local determinations, such as the distance‑ladder method anchored by Type Ia supernovae and Cepheid variables, give a higher H₀ (≈ 73 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹), whereas the value derived from the Cosmic Microwave Background (CMB) anisotropies within the standard ΛCDM framework is lower (≈ 67 km s⁻¹ Mpc⁻¹) [1][2]. This tension remains unresolved and may indicate uncharacterised systematics or a breakdown of the standard cosmological model.
